title: Gateway SDK integration + auth & env pair-programming lab
summary: AE + SE pair walked Cynosure engineering team through Redwood SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, auth patterns (API keys, SSO, KMS), sandbox environment setup, and a short live pairing session to run a sample generation and an embeddings job. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, certificate/VPC questions, and next steps for a pilot and security pack.
action_items: Jordan Park - Share sandbox API key + invite to Redwood console (sandbox) - due 2025-12-12
Maya Chen - Run small perf script and share tokenized cost estimate spreadsheet - due 2025-12-15
Alejandro Ruiz - Provide sample prompt set and typical sequence length distribution - due 2025-12-16
next_steps: Redwood to provide sandbox access and security pack
Customer to run two quick benchmarks and report latency/throughput
Follow-up technical deep dive scheduled (canary/rollout plan) - tentative 2025-12-18
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro - I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. With me is Maya our SE and Omar from DevEx. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Tom (CTO): Doing well, thanks. Excited to see the SDK flow, we want something that plugs into our pipeline fast.
[00:16] Maya (SE): Great, we'll do a short demo of both Python and TypeScript quickstarts, cover auth patterns, and then jump into a short pair-programming session where Alejandro or Priya can drive.
[00:27] Alejandro (Backend Lead): Sounds good. Our main constraints: latency under 200ms p95 for chat snippets, and data never leaves our VPC for regulated flows.
[00:34] Jordan (AE): Noted. We'll point out Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. For the pair session we'll use the sandbox hosted instance so you can see flow without dealing with VPC yet.
[00:44] Maya (SE): Ok jumping into code - first python quickstart. pip install redwood-sdk (note: transcript may say redwood-client in places) then set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var. Example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx.
[00:58] Priya (SRE): Quick question - for CI we can't have permanent secrets in plain env. Do you support short-lived keys or KMS integration?
[01:05] Maya (SE): Yes, we recommend using transient tokens from your secrets manager. We integrate with common KMS providers and provide guidance for CI: use the Redwood token broker or retrieve via KMS on build. We also support managed key wrapping for Private installs.
[01:19] Alejandro (Backend): When you say "redwood token broker" is that a hosted service or part of the Private package?
[01:25] Omar (DevEx): Good callout — token broker is part of the Hosted control plane, but for Private we provide a local token broker pattern and HSM/KMS connectors. Sometimes the transcriptors say K-V cache as k v cash, apologies for typos.
[01:39] Jordan (AE): We're going to show both a Python snippet and TypeScript. In TS we demo the npm package @redwood/inference. Set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY or use the SDK constructor with a token retrieved from your secret store.
[01:52] [00:02:00] Maya (SE): Live run — I'll call the text generation endpoint with a short prompt. Note there's streaming support; the example uses streaming to progressively render tokens in the UI.
[02:10] [00:02:10] Maya (SE): (typing) Okay I'm seeing streaming chunks, latency about 80ms for the first token in the sandbox, but note sandbox is best-effort and hosted infra varies.
[02:22] Alejandro (Backend): For production, what's typical p95 on hosted?
[02:28] Jordan (AE): For small models and tuned kernels, our Hosted p95 for single-turn gen is often sub-150ms in US regions, depends on model family and quantization. Dedicated pools give tighter guarantees with SLA.
[02:39] Priya (SRE): Security — we need audit logs and role separation. Does Redwood Console show token-level usage and per-route access?
[02:46] Maya (SE): Yes Console has RBAC and token-level cost/latency breakdowns. You can integrate with your SIEM, and all requests have trace IDs. For Private we deliver audit log exports and optional push to your log ingest.
[02:59] Tom (CTO): Data residency — our EU customers require data to remain in region. How do you ensure that?
[03:05] Jordan (AE): You can pin routes to region and model variants. For Private deployments it's fully customer-controlled. For Hosted we have region controls and contractual terms for data residency.
[03:18] [00:03:30] Maya (SE): Switching to SDK auth patterns — three main flows: 1) long-lived API key (not recommended for prod CI), 2) SSO/SAML for human users to access Console and issue scoped tokens, 3) brokered short-lived tokens for services.
[03:35] Priya (SRE): For SSO do you support SCIM/Okta provisioning?
[03:40] Maya (SE): Yes Okta and several IdPs, SCIM for user provisioning and role mapping.
[03:46] [00:04:15] Alejandro (Backend): Let's do the pair programming. I'll open the sample repo.
[03:50] Alejandro (Backend): (screen share noises) Found the TS quickstart, running npm install, then npm run dev.
[03:58] [00:05:00] Maya (SE): While that's spinning, note the quickstart has env.example showing REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENDPOINT (useful if you're targeting a dedicated cluster or private endpoint), and REDWOOD_REGION. For Private deployments you usually point at a VPC-internal endpoint like https://redwood-internal.company.local.
[04:17] [00:05:30] Alejandro (Backend): npm install threw a minor warning "node16 compatibility" (transcription might say note 16 vs 18). We're on node 18 so should be fine.
[04:26] Jordan (AE): If you see any runtime kernal errors (kernal/kernal spelled weird in transcript), it's usually a mismatch in the binary client; our SDK has fallbacks but let Maya know and she'll share a pinned version.
[04:38] [00:06:00] Maya (SE): Running a embeddings job now — small doc set. In Python the flow is: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); client.embeddings.create([...]) — text may show slight differences in auto transcript.
[04:58] Priya (SRE): Do embeddings consume a lot of tokens and cost? We plan vector search at scale.
[05:04] Maya (SE): Embeddings are per input token and per-dim cost. Optimize suggests batching inputs to reduce overhead and using our delta-quantized variants for cheaper storage. We'll send the Optimize recommendations based on your sequence length distribution.
[05:20] [00:07:00] Alejandro (Backend): We have a question about canary rollouts — we use feature flags to route traffic. Does Redwood have rollout primitives?
[05:27] Jordan (AE): Yes Console supports canary deploys, traffic splitting by route and automatic fallback to a stable model or older quantized variant if errors increase. Good to plan that into your release process.
[05:40] [00:07:45] Tom (CTO): Any limitations on request sizes? We send long docs sometimes.
[05:46] Maya (SE): We have sequence length limits per model and configured token windows. For large docs we recommend chunking and embeddings + retrieval pipeline. Also KV cache strategies help for chat. Sometimes the transcript shows KV as K V cash, ignore that.
[06:00] [00:08:30] Alejandro (Backend): Pairing now — I ran the TS dev server and hit the local page, calling the SDK with our sandbox key. I see the sample generation.
[06:09] Maya (SE): Nice. Can you try toggling streaming vs non-streaming? The SDK param is stream:true.
[06:16] Alejandro (Backend): Streaming is working, partial tokens show up. Latency seems fine.
[06:23] [00:09:00] Priya (SRE): Logging — how do we correlate requests to our system? Do you return trace IDs?
[06:29] Maya (SE): Yes every request returns a trace id and the Console surfaces traces and per-token timing. You can push the logs to your SIEM or pull via API.
[06:37] [00:09:45] Jordan (AE): Quick note on pricing — Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is committed capacity. We'll send a cost model with token estimates based on your benchmark.
[06:48] [00:10:20] Alejandro (Backend): We have an internal compliance ask around encryption in transit and at rest.
[06:53] Maya (SE): All hosted traffic is TLS encrypted in transit; at rest we encrypt with customer-managed keys via KMS for Private, and for Dedicated you can elect managed or bring-your-own-key on some tiers.
[07:04] [00:11:00] Tom (CTO): For the pilot we want to test both hosted sandbox and a small dedicated pool. How quick is a dedicated spin-up?
[07:11] Jordan (AE): For small pools we can provision within days, larger reserved capacity is a contractual process that takes longer. We'll include that in the next step doc.
[07:20] [00:11:45] Maya (SE): A quick demo of Optimize — we've got a small recommendations page that suggests batching window, quantization profiles, and caching opportunities. For embeddings heavy workloads it often recommends smaller batch sizes to avoid latency spikes and delta-quantization for storage.
[07:36] Alejandro (Backend): Can we run the Optimize tool against our sample workload?
[07:40] Maya (SE): Yes, bring us your sample prompts and token histograms and we'll run Optimize and return recommended configs. That's actually one of the action items.
[07:49] [00:12:30] (Crosstalk)
[07:52] Priya (SRE): Network — if we go Private, will Redwood require outbound connectivity to control plane?
[07:58] Omar (DevEx): For Private we offer both fully air-gapped options and hybrid where control plane still calls home for updates; depends on your compliance box. We'll share the Private deployment matrix in the security pack.
[08:11] [00:13:00] Jordan (AE): Let's capture next steps — we'll hand off sandbox creds and the security pack. Maya will run the perf script and produce the baseline numbers.
[08:20] Tom (CTO): Good. Also price and SLA for a small dedicated pool — please include expected p95 and commit sizes.
[08:27] Jordan (AE): We'll do that.
[08:31] [00:13:45] Alejandro (Backend): One more quick SDK nit — our frontend is in React/TS and we want client-side tokenless flows. Any recommendations?
[08:39] Maya (SE): Don't embed secrets in client. Use a token-exchange endpoint in your backend that mints short-lived tokens scoped to the operation. We have examples in the repo: exchange endpoint that calls Redwood and returns a transient token for the browser.
[08:52] [00:14:30] Alejandro (Backend): Noted.
[08:55] [00:14:45] Maya (SE): Wrapping up pairing — Alejandro hit the two sample routes, embeddings and generation. We'll send the small perf harness and the cost-est spreadsheet.
[09:06] Priya (SRE): Any blockers on data flow for the pilot?
[09:10] Jordan (AE): None from our side. For the pilot we'll need an NDA addendum for EU residency and a starter SOW for dedicated if you pick that path.
[09:19] Tom (CTO): Ok let's get the sandbox tomorrow and schedule the follow-up deep-dive next week.
[09:24] Jordan (AE): Great. Recap of action items and owners in the notes. Thanks everyone.
[09:30] (meeting ends)
